- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and should reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates and should adjust upward, especially if recent prices are trending down.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and should apply a downward correction in the next 3–5 periods.  
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5) — increase baseline forecast by 2–5% in such contexts.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model may be lagging — apply a “mean reversion” adjustment by adding 1–3% to forecast for next period.  
- When sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.3), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast slope or add a “sentiment lag” buffer.  
- Forecast should not be linearly extrapolated from recent history — especially if sentiment is volatile — introduce a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” to dampen momentum.
